business_summary: InterGlobe Aviation is an airline operator. Revenue grew about 16% a year over three years to FY26. Operating margin is 14.17%, but FY26 net profit was negative at Rs 2,391.9 crore, and borrowings are 11.15 times equity. Return on capital is low.
why_own: The case rests on revenue still growing at a double-digit rate while operating margin holds, but the company is loss-making (FY26 net profit -Rs 2,391.9 crore, trailing four quarters -Rs 4,805.8 crore) and no investor documents were supplied, so this thesis is thin and metric-only. It is a bet that operating performance can eventually cover the heavy debt burden, and the evidence does not yet show that.

drivers.statement: Revenue keeps compounding at a double-digit rate (3-year CAGR currently about 16%).
Operating margin holds at or near the current 14%, after rising 2.17 percentage points over three years.
Leverage does not climb further from 11.15 times equity.
Interest cover, currently below 1 at 0.67 times, does not weaken further. Improvement towards 1 or higher is what the thesis needs.
Trailing four-quarter net profit should not be negative. (added by code: currently -4805.8.)

kill_criteria.description: All of the last four reported quarters are loss-making (currently three of four).

risks.statement: The company is loss-making: FY26 net profit was -Rs 2,391.9 crore, the trailing four quarters total -Rs 4,805.8 crore, and 3 of the last 4 quarters were losses. Profit growth, ROE, cash flow to profit and P/E are all undefined.
Debt is very high at 11.15 times equity, interest cover is 0.67 times, and ROCE is only 4.7%. Earnings do not currently cover interest.
The stock trades at 25.55 times book value while losing money. There is no profit-based valuation anchor, since P/E and the comparison with its own history are both unavailable.

skeptic_counter_case: The thesis bets that operating performance will eventually cover the debt, but the evidence shows it is not doing so. A 14.17% operating margin and 16% revenue growth still produced a loss of Rs 2,391.9 crore, with interest cover at 0.67x. It would be wrong if growth slows toward the 8% break line while margin slips and debt stays near 11x equity, because the equity base is thin and the stock trades at 25.55x book. The thresholds are lenient: they mark the thesis OK while earnings already fail to cover interest. K1 only trips once all four quarters are losses, and three already are. What would change this view: Trailing four-quarter net profit turning positive, with interest cover (PBT plus interest, divided by interest) at or above 1x while debt/equity stays at or below 11x.
